input.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Checks that the score sheet's columns line up.
#
# score() in finish.c prints one line per thing the player did, each a
# format string ending in %5d, and every one of them is meant to put its
# number in the same column. Nothing enforced that. The plural Romulan
# line spent years a space short, so a winning player's surrendered-ship
# count sat one column left of everything under it (#62) -- on the score
# sheet a player is most likely to read, since surrendered Romulans only
# count on a win.
#
# It went unnoticed because no test could see it. The recordings in
# tests/golden are the only place a score sheet is written down, and
# until a game was won there was none with a Romulan line in it at all.
#
# So this reads the format strings themselves rather than any output. It
# is the only way to reach the singular forms: "1 Romulan ship
# surrendered" needs exactly one Romulan left alive at the end, and a
# novice game starts with two or three, so no journey can produce one
# without hunting Romulans first. Both forms of all thirteen lines are
# checked here, which is what #62 asked for.
#
# What this cannot see, and golden does: the two lines assembled from
# pieces rather than printed from one format -- the winning bonus, built
# from proutn fragments and a skill name, and the killed penalty, a bare
# literal. tests/golden/won.txt records both at the same column as the
# rest.
#
# Usage: score.sh /path/to/repo/root

set -u

ROOT="${1:-.}"
FINISH="$ROOT/finish.c"

# Where the number ends on every line of the sheet. Not a number the
# code declares anywhere -- it is the shape all but one of the lines
# already had, and the one that the recordings show.
WIDTH=47

fails=0
fail() {
	printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2
	fails=$((fails + 1))
}

if [ ! -f "$FINISH" ]; then
	echo "FAIL: $FINISH not found" >&2
	exit 1
fi

# Every string literal that ends in a %5d field, with the conversions
# replaced by the width they print: %6d and %6.2f are six columns, %5d
# is five. A ternary puts two literals on one line, so the line is split
# on quotes and every other field taken.
report=$(awk -v want="$WIDTH" '
	/%5d\\n/ {
		n = split($0, part, "\"")
		for (i = 2; i <= n; i += 2) {
			lit = part[i]
			if (lit !~ /%5d\\n/) continue
			s = lit
			gsub(/\\n/, "", s)
			gsub(/%6\.2f/, "XXXXXX", s)
			gsub(/%6d/, "XXXXXX", s)
			gsub(/%5d/, "YYYYY", s)
			if (length(s) != want)
				printf "%d:%d:%s\n", FNR, length(s), lit
			seen++
		}
	}
	END { printf "count:%d\n", seen+0 }
' "$FINISH")

count=$(echo "$report" | sed -n 's/^count:\([0-9]*\)$/\1/p')
echo "$report" | grep -v '^count:' | while IFS=: read -r line width lit; do
	[ -n "${line:-}" ] || continue
	printf 'FAIL: finish.c:%s puts its number at column %s, not %s -- "%s"\n' \
		"$line" "$width" "$WIDTH" "$lit" >&2
done
# The loop above runs in a subshell, so its failures are counted here.
bad=$(echo "$report" | grep -vc '^count:' || true)
[ "$bad" = 0 ] || fails=$((fails + bad))

# A count guards the guard. If the shape of these lines ever changes so
# that the pattern stops matching, every line would "align" by not being
# looked at, and this test would pass while checking nothing.
MINLINES=24
if [ -z "${count:-}" ] || [ "$count" -lt "$MINLINES" ]; then
	fail "only ${count:-0} score lines matched, expected at least $MINLINES -- has score() changed shape?"
fi

if [ "$fails" -ne 0 ]; then
	printf '\n%d score-sheet column problem(s).\n' "$fails" >&2
	exit 1
fi

printf 'score OK (%s lines, column %s)\n' "$count" "$WIDTH"

gh issue create --title "Assert the score sheet's columns from the compiled game, not from its source text" --label "good first issue" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

`tests/score.sh` (added with #62) holds every score-sheet format string
in `finish.c` to column 47. It works, and it reaches what no journey can
— ten of the twelve singular forms and four of the five skill labels
appear in no recording — but it does so by scraping C source text, and
its own header admits the two costs:

- **It never sees the compiled game.** It re-implements printf width
  semantics in awk (`%6d` → 6, `%6.2f` → 6). If `proutf` ever stopped
  honouring those widths, only `golden` would notice.
- **It degrades under reformatting.** A literal split by C string
  concatenation drops out of the scan. That was a live false pass during
  review — a floor of 24 let it through silently — and it is now guarded
  by an exact count of 27, which is a tripwire rather than a fix. The
  twelve dual-form `proutf` lines are 118-122 columns, so "wrap the long
  lines" is a plausible future chore that trips it.

## Suggested approach

Hoist the literals into a table `score()` indexes:

```c
static const char *const score_lines[] = { ... };
```

Then assert in C — `tests/test_rules.c` is the existing home for a C
test, or a new one — by `snprintf`-ing each entry with representative
arguments and checking the result is 47 columns.

That reaches every singular form and every skill label, uses printf's
real semantics instead of a model of them, is immune to how the source
is wrapped, and deletes the awk.

Worth deciding while there what to do about the two lines the table
cannot hold as single formats: the winning bonus, assembled from a
prefix, a skill label and a tail, and the `Penalty for getting yourself
killed` literal, which carries no conversion at all.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The column invariant is asserted against what the compiled game
      prints, not against the text of `finish.c`.
- [ ] Every singular and plural form is still covered, and the skill
      labels with them.
- [ ] `tests/score.sh` is deleted, or reduced to whatever the C test
      cannot reach, and `CMakeLists.txt` updated to match.

Raised by the `code-review` sub-agent while reviewing #62, which is where
the scraping test came from. Follow the workflow in
[AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).
EOF
)"

#62 is closed — merged as `dbcaa63`, branch deleted, tree clean.

**The fix is one space.** The plural Romulan surrender line printed its number at column 46; the other 26 score lines, the total, the bonus and the penalty all use 47. A winning player saw a digit hanging one column left of everything under it, on the one score sheet worth reading — surrendered Romulans score nothing unless the game was won. `won.txt` re-recorded; the diff is that single line, exactly as the issue predicted.

**The test was the real work.** `tests/score.sh` reads the format strings out of `score()` rather than any output, because a journey only prints the line its game earns: ten of the twelve singular forms and four of the five skill labels appear in no recording at all. `1 Romulan ship surrendered` needs exactly one Romulan alive at the end, where a novice game starts with two or three — unreachable.

**Two rounds of review earned their keep, and I'd flag this as the session's lesson.** As I first wrote it, the test counted rows in a window that ran past the block it meant to read; claimed `golden` covered a bonus line it records one fifth of; named the wrong fixture for the killed penalty (`won.txt` *can't* contain it — the ship survives); and its floor of 24 matched lines let the reviewer walk a genuine false pass through it. Splitting one literal across two source lines dropped a format out of the scan and it still printed `OK`. That's the fourth vacuous assertion this session — the rule added in `0a075a5` is earning its place faster than I'd like.

I reproduced both the false pass and its fix rather than accepting the report, and the count is now exact.

**Two things I'd want you to know:**

- **#76 is filed**, and it's the honest limit of what I built. The test models printf widths in awk and never sees the compiled game, and it degrades if those 120-column ternaries are ever wrapped. The right shape — hoist the literals into a table, assert with real `snprintf` — touches `score()`, which is too much for a one-space fix.
- **`ui-review` found something out of scope I did *not* file:** on a plain `quit` the game prints no score sheet, then immediately asks "Do you want your score recorded?" — a number the player was never shown. It predates everything here, and by the step 9 bar it's terse 1978 UX rather than a defect that misleads. Say the word if you'd rather it were tracked.

Review branch `fix/tui-resize-repaint` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek (uncommitted, diff against `main`). This closes #46 and it is squarely in your remit — it changes how the full-screen interface behaves under the player's hands.

What changed in `tui.c`:
1. `tui_getch()` (the paging pause) — on `KEY_RESIZE` it now calls `tui_refresh_panels()` and waits again, instead of silently swallowing the resize and leaving the old screen until the player pressed a key. Safe there because curses reports the resize *by returning from* `wgetch`, so nothing is reading the screen at that moment.
2. `tui_readline()` — `wgetnstr` is replaced by a hand-rolled reader that takes one keystroke at a time: printable ASCII, backspace, Enter, Ctrl-D, and `KEY_RESIZE` handled between keystrokes. This is what lets a resize be redrawn mid-prompt, and it keeps the partially typed line, which `wgetnstr` discarded. Ctrl-D on an empty line now ends the session on its own keystroke instead of needing an Enter after it.

`tests/tui.sh` gains three sections: resize during a pause, resize while an answer is half typed, and Ctrl-D.

Please be hard on this from the player's side — a hand-rolled line editor is exactly where a terminal game gets subtly worse:
- **Typing feel.** Does the prompt behave as a player expects at 80x24 and 72x24? Backspace at the start of a line, backspace past the prompt (it must not eat the prompt or the panel border), a very long answer that wraps or hits the buffer limit, fast typing, holding a key down.
- **Keys that are no longer accepted.** The reader takes printable ASCII only, so arrow keys, Home/End, Delete, Tab and pasted text with control characters are now ignored rather than inserted. Is any of that a regression a player would feel? Pasting a command is the case I am least sure about.
- **The resize behaviour itself** at both sizes, during a pause and mid-typing, including shrinking (not just growing) and a resize below the 72x24 minimum.
- **Ctrl-C, Ctrl-U, Ctrl-W** and anything else a terminal user might reflexively press at a prompt.
- Whether the paging pause still needs exactly one keystroke, and whether a resize can still page away unread text.

input.message:
All three should-fixes addressed, plus the comment nit. Please re-review — particularly the shrink case, which is the one I want you to try to break again.

**1 (shrinking loses the prompt and unread text).** You were right and this was the serious one. `wresize` keeps the top of the window, so the rows it drops are exactly where the newest text and the prompt live. `make_windows()` now scrolls the difference away *before* resizing when the message window is losing height, so the oldest rows go instead of the newest:

```c
int oldh = getmaxy(wmsg);
if (msgh < oldh)
    wscrl(wmsg, oldh - msgh);
```

Verified at 100x30 → 72x24 during a `help move` pause: before the fix all four bottom lines including `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` were gone; now the prompt and the three lines of help above it survive, and one Space still advances exactly one page rather than skipping the text that used to be discarded.

**2 (backspace across a wrapped answer).** Fixed — `erase_one()` now steps to the end of the row above when the cursor is at column 0, instead of returning and letting the buffer and the screen disagree. The `len > 0` guard is what keeps it off the prompt, since it can never erase more characters than were typed.

**3 (Ctrl-U).** Restored — it erases the whole line, screen and buffer together, with a comment saying it was the one piece of line editing `wgetnstr` had that this reader would otherwise have dropped.

**7 (the stale comment).** `tui_getch`'s note no longer says "the line read below" — `tui_readline` is above it, and it is no longer something you cannot repaint under.

I also took the README suggestion: one sentence saying the display follows the terminal, including mid-answer.

**Something you should know before you re-test.** While checking the shrink fix I hit `COMMAND> sc` where `srsc` had been typed, and chased it as a possible new bug. It reproduces identically on a pre-fix binary built from `main`, and the cause is mundane: `help move` has more pages than the four Spaces I was sending, so the `s` and `r` answered the remaining pause prompts before the game reached the command prompt. Not a regression, and not timing — a three-second settle makes no difference. Flagging it so you do not spend the time I did.

**6 (sub-minimum garbling)** is filed as #78 rather than fixed here: it predates the change, and deciding between "say the terminal is too small" and "genuinely clip" is a design call that deserves its own slice. The issue records that #46 made it more visible rather than caused it.

**4 and 5** (ignored keys; the silent buffer cap) will be called out in the commit as deliberate, as you asked.

The three new test sections still pass on the fixed build and all five of their assertions still fail against a pre-fix binary. I have not yet added a shrink case to the tests — tell me whether you want it in `tui.sh` given the pause section already resizes, or whether the growth case plus the manual shrink evidence is enough.

input.message:
Your finding 1 was deeper than either of us thought, and my first two fixes for it were wrong. The state has changed enough since my last message that I would ignore that one and re-test from scratch — especially the shrink.

**What was actually happening.** Curses clips the message window when *it* processes the resize, and it does that before handing the game `KEY_RESIZE`. So the bottom rows — the newest text, the prompt — are gone before any of the game's code runs. I proved it by instrumenting a scratch build: at the moment the game is told, `getmaxy(wmsg)` already reads 24 where the window had been 27.

That killed two attempts:
- scrolling the height difference away before resizing — the content sits at the *top* until the conversation has filled the window, so this threw away everything and left a blank panel (100x30 → 72x24 looked fixed, 120x40 → 72x24 went blank);
- doing the same before `resize_term` via a `TIOCGWINSZ` ioctl — too late as well, for the reason above.

**What works.** `tui.c` now keeps `curline`, the text since the last newline, updated in `tui_puts`/`tui_puts_slow`. After a resize the repaint reads the row the cursor is on and reprints that line only if the clip took it — so the prompt comes back on a shrink and is not duplicated on a growth. `tui_readline` re-echoes its buffer after that, so the answer follows the prompt back onto the screen.

Measured across five directions, all showing the prompt exactly once and the page text intact: 80x24→120x40, 100x30→72x24, 120x40→72x24, 80x24→72x24, 72x24→100x30. The 120x40→72x24 case is the one that was blank.

**Your other findings:** backspace across a wrapped line steps to the row above now; Ctrl-U restored; the stale `tui_getch` comment fixed; README sentence added.

**Tests.** `tui.sh` has a shrink block as you asked (120x40 → 72x24, the case that failed). Seven of its eight new assertions fail against a pre-fix binary and all pass against this one. The eighth — "shrinking paged away unread text" — passes pre-fix too, because the clip took the prompt and left that text; I kept it as a property worth holding and said so in the comment rather than let it look like evidence.

Please re-run your typing-feel checks as well as the resize ones: `curline` is written on every output line now, and the reader re-echoes into the window after a repaint, so I would like both paths re-tested rather than assumed. #78 is filed for the sub-minimum garbling.

input.message:
All three reproduced defects fixed, and one of them had a cause worth telling you. Please re-test.

**1 (answer echoed twice).** `restore_curline()` now reports whether it actually wrote the line out again, and `tui_readline` re-echoes its buffer only in that case. Measured across all six of your directions with `srsc` pending — 80x24→120x40, 80x24→100x30, 72x24→100x30, 80x24→72x24, 100x30→72x24, 120x40→72x24 — every one now reads ` COMMAND> srsc` exactly once. Your point about the test pattern was right and it is now anchored (`'COMMAND> *srsc *$'`), with a comment saying an unanchored one matched `srscsrsc` happily while the bug was live.

**2 (setup questions duplicated).** Your diagnosis of the mechanism was right but the root cause was mine, one level down: the reader writes the newline on Enter straight to the window, bypassing `note_out`, so `curline` never ended and grew across prompts. The remembered line became "Would you like a regular, tournament, or frozen game?Type in tournament number-", which exists on no single row, so the search failed and appended a copy. The reader now tells `note_out` about that newline. Both blockers fixed, and your suggested fix for the first was better than what I had — it deleted a flag rather than adding a condition. Please try to break it again.

**1 (cursor in front of the answer).** Taken exactly as you proposed: `restore_curline()` always leaves the cursor at the end of `curline`, and `tui_readline` re-echoes `buf` unconditionally from there. Where the answer survived on screen it writes the same characters over themselves; where it did not it supplies them. `line_restored` is gone. Measured by typing `srsc`, resizing, then typing `an`: all six directions now read ` COMMAND> srscan` — 80x24→120x40, 80x24→100x30, 72x24→100x30, 80x24→72x24, 100x30→72x24, 120x40→72x24.

**2 (matching an older prompt).** A match now counts only as the last thing on the screen: nothing but blanks after it on its row, and nothing but blank rows below. ` COMMAND> damages` fails both and is treated as missing, so the line is reprinted at the bottom. Measured with `status`, `damages`, `rest 1` behind it, then typing `ch` after the shrink — 100x30→100x24, 80x30→80x24, 100x30→72x24, 120x40→72x24 all put it on a fresh prompt at the bottom.

**Tests.** Both of your suggested assertions are in: the line after the answer is finished (`'COMMAND> *srscan *$'`), and a new block that runs two commands before shrinking and asserts the last non-blank line is the live prompt with nothing after it, then finishes the command and checks it ran. Nine assertions now fail against a pre-fix binary and all pass against this one.

**Re-verified after the change, since these came from earlier rounds:** the doubled answer (once in all six), duplicated setup questions (one copy on growth), the chopped line (`current warp factor (see "WARP FACTOR").` whole), and the pause across three directions with one prompt and the page text intact.

**On the README (your nit 3):** with finding 2 fixed the sentence "a terminal that gets smaller keeps the question and the answer" should now be true — please confirm that, since you are better placed to judge it than I am.

Full `ctest` is rerunning in both build types. If this round is clean I will take it to the verifier and code-review; if it is not, I would rather hear it now than after it lands.

`tui.c` now keeps `pending_answer`, set by `tui_readline` around its `tui_refresh_panels()` call and NULL at a pause. `restore_curline()` builds the line it expects to see — `curline` plus whatever the reader has echoed — and looks for *that* on the last non-blank row, requiring blanks only after the pair. A surviving prompt-plus-answer is recognised and nothing is drawn; the cursor still goes to the end of `curline`, so the unconditional re-echo writes the same characters over themselves. The comment states the invariant in your words: the bottom of the conversation is the game's unfinished line and the player's unfinished answer, and the restore compares against both.

Measured, with `srsc` pending:
- one prompt in all six directions — 80x24→120x40, 80x24→100x30, 72x24→100x30, 80x24→72x24, 100x30→72x24, 120x40→72x24, each still reading ` COMMAND> srsc`;
- the twelve-step widen drag that stood up eight copies: **one** prompt, and finishing with `an` runs `srscan`;
- six alternating resizes: **one** prompt.

Your point about the tests was right and the count assertion is in: after the resize with an answer pending, `screen | grep -c 'COMMAND>'` must be 1, with a comment saying the line-shape check cannot see a duplicate because the last copy looks perfectly correct. Nine assertions fail against a pre-fix binary, all pass here, and `ctest` is rerunning in both build types.

Two things I would like you to be unkind about, since this is the fourth round and each has moved the failure somewhere new:
1. The setup conversation with an answer pending, in both directions — that is where the pending-answer path and the not-yet-full window overlap, and both have surprised me before.
2. Anything where `curline` and the echoed answer are not adjacent on one row: an answer long enough to wrap, and a prompt long enough to wrap on its own at 72 columns.

Four of your five wrap cases are fixed; the fifth I have left and documented, and I would like you to say whether you accept that.

**What I did.** Your multi-row join did not work on its own: a width change makes curses re-lay the rows and pad them, so the joined text has blanks in the middle and never matches. What does work is not searching at all when there is nothing to find — a terminal that only grew clipped nothing, so `sync_size` now calls the restore only when `LINES` or `COLS` went *down*. That closes 72x24→100x30 with `emeritus maybe` pending, 80x24→100x30 with 75 characters typed, 80x30→110x30, and the twelve-step widen drag, which is now one prompt where it was four.

That change also broke the re-echo and the suite caught it: skipping the restore leaves the cursor after the answer, so re-echoing doubled it. The re-echo is now conditional on the restore having actually repositioned the cursor (`cursor_at_prompt`), which is the honest version of the flag I deleted two rounds ago — it means "the cursor is at the end of the prompt", not "the line was reprinted".

**The one I left: a width shrink that clips a wrapped pair** (110x30 → 80x30 with 75 characters typed). The line genuinely no longer fits, curses truncates it, and the restore writes a fresh copy below the stump. Measured: the live prompt is the last thing on screen, holds the whole answer re-wrapped at the new width, and finishing it runs the command. #46 asks for the answer to be preserved or clearly restarted rather than half eaten, and this is the second of those, so I have documented it in `restore_curline` rather than chase it further. This is the fifth round and the last two findings have both come from the same place — the restore trying to work out what is on screen. If you see a sixth of that shape, say so plainly and I will stop trying to detect it and simply reprint on every clip, duplicates and all.

input.prompt:
Code-review branch `fix/tui-resize-repaint` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek: the diff against `main` plus all staged, unstaged and untracked files. Three files: `tui.c`, `tests/tui.sh`, `README.md`.

Closes #46 (a resize during a prompt or pause left the display stale until the player pressed a key). This has been through five rounds of `ui-review` and one `verifier` pass; both found real defects each round, so please assume there is a sixth and look for it.

What the change does in `tui.c`:
- `tui_getch` repaints on `KEY_RESIZE` instead of swallowing it. Safe because curses reports the resize *by returning from* `wgetch`.
- `wgetnstr` is replaced by a hand-rolled reader: printable ASCII, backspace (with `erase_one` stepping to the row above at a wrap), Ctrl-U, Ctrl-D (now ends the session on its own keystroke), Enter, and `KEY_RESIZE` handled between keystrokes.
- The hard part: **curses clips the message window when it processes the resize, before the game is told**, so a shrink destroys the prompt and the typed answer before any of this code runs. So `tui.c` keeps `curline` (the game's line since the last newline, recorded in `tui_puts`/`tui_puts_slow`) and `pending_answer` (what the reader has echoed), and `restore_curline()` puts them back when they were clipped.
- `sync_size` skips the restore entirely when the terminal only grew (nothing can have been clipped), and passes the old message width when the width shrank so the stump's height is computed arithmetically rather than searched for.
- `cursor_at_prompt` tells the reader whether the repaint repositioned the cursor, so the re-echo does not double the answer.

Please review as an expert in C, ncurses and POSIX shell. Specifically:
- **The state machine.** `curline`, `curlen`, `pending_answer`, `cursor_at_prompt` are four pieces of static state maintained across three functions. Is there a path that leaves them inconsistent — an early return, a second game (`tui_gameover`/`tui_clearmsg`), a resize during `tui_puts_slow`, or a game line longer than `curline`'s 255 bytes?
- **`restore_curline`.** The row arithmetic (`start`, `i / width`, `i % width`, `maxy - rows`), the `strncat` bound, and whether `wclrtoeol` over the bottom rows can erase something that should have survived.
- **The reader's contract**: `buf`/`buflen` from `readinput()`, the `"\n"` append, the `room = buflen-2` guard.
- Whether any of this can affect **plain mode** (it must not) or the non-resize TUI path.
- The tests: are the new assertions in `tests/tui.sh` meaningful, and does anything there pass against a broken build?
Give an explicit approve / request-changes verdict.

input.message:
All five taken, and finding 1 was a genuine sixth defect of the shape the earlier rounds kept producing. Please re-review.

**1 (anchored to the bottom rather than to the line).** Fixed as you suggested: the scan that finds the last non-blank row now keeps it in `last`, and the rewrite anchors there — `r = (last >= 0 ? last : maxy - 1) - rows + 1`. When the height shrank, `last` is the bottom row and the behaviour is unchanged; when it did not, the stump is erased in place and there is no duplicate. Your three reproductions all give one copy now: 110x40 setup question with an 82-character answer narrowed to 76; the 120x24 → 76x34 corner drag; and the twelve-step narrowing drag.

I also took the over-count: `rows` is now `total == 0 ? 1 : (total - 1) / oldmsgw + 1`, so a line that fills its last row exactly no longer claims an extra row and rubs out live history above the stump. Checked with a 72-character answer at a 82-column message window shrinking to 74 — one copy, briefing still on screen.

**2 (no test types an answer and then shrinks).** That gap is why this survived six rounds, and it is now covered: a new `shrink typing` section types an answer long enough to wrap at the narrower width, narrows 100x30 → 76x30, and asserts exactly one prompt, the whole answer still present, and the conversation still on screen. Ten assertions now fail against a pre-fix binary.

Worth recording: my first version of that test asserted the prompt and answer as one joined string and failed against a *correct* build. The message window starts at column one, so joining the wrapped rows puts the left margin in the middle of the answer. It counts the characters instead now, with a comment saying why.

**3 (`\r` in `note_out`).** Fixed — a carriage return ends the line as a newline does, with your `pause()` reasoning in the comment.

**4 (`cursor_at_prompt` reset).** Now cleared in the `KEY_RESIZE` branch immediately before the repaint, so the invariant is local and does not depend on `sync_size` having taken its resized path.

**5 (`want`'s 160).** Commented, naming `readinput()`'s 128-byte callers and the 126 the reader can fill — and, in the same note, why `onscreen` and `row_blank`'s row are deliberately narrower than a wide terminal, with the invariant that makes that safe and the condition that would break it.

`ctest` is rerunning in both build types; `tui.sh` is green and `shellcheck -s sh` clean.

A resize was noticed and then sat on. The panels were rebuilt at the
next prompt, so dragging the window while the game waited on "hit space
bar to continue" left them the old size with the new columns empty
beside them, for as long as the player took to press a key -- a game
that looked like it had stopped. Typing was worse: wgetnstr returned
ERR on the resize and threw the half-typed answer away with it, so the
prompt looked untouched and the game got only whatever was typed after.

tui_getch can repaint where the old comment said it could not: curses
reports the resize by returning from wgetch, so nothing is reading the
screen at that moment. The line reader now works the same way, a
keystroke at a time instead of wgetnstr, which is what lets a resize be
handled between them -- and it keeps its own buffer, so nothing is lost.
Ctrl-D ends the session on its own keystroke now rather than needing an
Enter after it, backspace steps back a row on a wrapped answer, and
Ctrl-U clears the line, which wgetnstr did for us before.

The hard half is that curses clips the message window when it processes
the resize, and it does that before handing the game KEY_RESIZE. By the
time the game is told, the bottom rows are gone -- and on a shrink those
rows are the prompt and the answer. Two attempts at scrolling ahead of
it failed for the same reason: the clip has already happened. So the
game keeps the line it is part way through writing, and puts it back
when it went. Where the terminal only grew nothing can have been
clipped and none of this runs; where it lost columns the stump's height
is arithmetic from the old width, and those rows are rubbed out and
rewritten in place, anchored to the last row with anything on it rather
than to the bottom of the window -- the setup conversation and anything
after a clearscreen sit mid-window, where a bottom anchor left a stump

cursor in the history, and copies that stacked one per step of a drag.

the build before this one.

content.text:
#46 is closed — merged as `66c8ca6`, all four CI legs green including both macOS pty runs, branch deleted, tree clean.

**What it does now.** Resize the terminal at any point and the display follows immediately — during a pause, mid-answer, growing or shrinking — and both the question and the half-typed answer survive. Ctrl-D ends the session on its own keystroke, backspace works across a wrapped answer, Ctrl-U clears the line.

**The finding that shaped the whole thing:** ncurses clips the message window when *it* processes the resize, before the game is ever told. By the time `KEY_RESIZE` arrives the prompt is already gone. Two of my fixes failed for exactly that reason before I instrumented a build and saw `getmaxy(wmsg)` already reading the new size. That's why the game now keeps the line it's writing and puts it back, rather than trying to preserve what's on screen.

**This was the most expensive thing in the session, and honestly so.** Six review rounds found six distinct defects in the hand-rolled reader — a doubled echo that made the screen disagree with the buffer, duplicated setup questions, a line chopped mid-word, a cursor left in front of the answer, a search matching an older prompt and parking the cursor in the command history, and copies stacking one per drag step. Each was real and player-visible; none would have been caught by the tests I'd written at the time.

The seventh finding is the one I'd single out: `code-review` tested *my test* by building a reverted-anchor binary, and the suite still passed. My shrink-while-typing case typed at the command prompt, where the window is already full — so the two anchorings compute the same row and a reverted fix sails through. The setup conversation is where they differ. That's the rule from `0a075a5` applied to me by someone else, and it's the fifth vacuous assertion this session.

Eleven assertions now fail against the pre-fix build. Plain mode and the golden recordings are byte-identical; 29 `tui` runs under load found no flakes; ASan/UBSan clean.

**Two things I deliberately did not fix**, both reproducing on `main`: the layout below 72x24 (**#78**, filed) and a stray glyph in the message window's unowned right-hand column — `ui-review` initially attributed that to me, then retracted after reproducing it on `main`.

The tracker now has no issues about the game itself. All six remaining are process integrity: **#65, #66, #71, #72** from the workflow work, plus **#76** (assert the score columns from the compiled game) and **#78**.
What is each one of those?

content.text:
All six are `good first issue`, and all six came out of this session. They split cleanly into two groups.

**The game and its tests**

- **#78 — below 72x24 the panels overlap instead of clipping.** `make_windows()` says in a comment that a too-small terminal "keeps their size and the screen clips, which is ugly." It doesn't clip — at 40x14 the status panel bleeds through the quadrant box (`xorWarp Fact`, `xLeTime Left`) and the message window collapses to one row. Pre-existing, but #46 made it *live*: the display now repaints while you're still dragging, so you see the mess repeatedly instead of once. The decision to make is whether sub-minimum should say "terminal too small" or genuinely clip.

- **#76 — assert the score columns from the compiled game, not its source text.** `tests/score.sh` holds every score-sheet format string to column 47 by scraping `finish.c` with awk. It works, and it reaches what no journey can (ten of twelve singular forms, four of five skill labels), but it re-implements printf's width rules in awk and never sees the compiled binary — and it degrades if those 120-column ternaries are ever wrapped. The fix is a `static const char *const` table plus a C test using real `snprintf`.

**The review machinery** — these exist because the workflow changes this session created gaps in themselves:

- **#65 — nothing checks AGENTS.md's workflow numbering.** `tests/instructions.sh` only verifies the file exists, exceeds 2000 bytes, and has the workflow heading. Insert a step and every "see step 9" reference silently rots. I renumbered three steps this session and checked all of it by hand. Later extended to cover step 6 quoting the section title verbatim.

- **#66 — a player-visible fix gets no second look from `ui-review`.** Steps 7 and 8 each say to rerun after addressing findings; step 6 doesn't. So a fix to wording or layout is never re-judged by the only reviewer qualified to judge it. Given how the #46 rounds went, I'd rate this the highest-value one here.

- **#71 — `ui-review`'s own description contradicts AGENTS.md.** Its frontmatter still says "invoke after the main agent completes an implementation pass," unconditionally, while the workflow now scopes it to changes that can alter what a player sees. That `description` field drives auto-delegation, so it isn't cosmetic. A comment later added that `verifier.md` has the same shape of problem — it asserts an ordering ("after `ui-review`") that may no longer hold.

- **#72 — nothing checks whether a skipped `ui-review` was owed.** The sharpest of the four, and it came from asking `code-review` to argue against a rule I'd written for my own convenience. Skipping is disclosed in the commit and PR body — but `code-review` runs *before* the commit exists, and no reviewer has a mandate to ask. So scoping an absolute rule into a judgement call put the author in sole charge of the one pass the author is tempted to skip.

If you want a recommendation: **#66** and **#72** are the pair worth doing together — they're the same hole from two sides (no re-review after a UI fix; no audit of a skipped UI review), and both are a clause or two of AGENTS.md plus possibly a line in `.claude/agents/`. **#78** is the only one a player would ever notice.
Lets do 66 and 72 next

Both are the same hole from two sides, and #72's fix has to reference the rule #66 adds — so I'll do them as one slice and say so plainly in the PR, rather than land a rule and immediately amend it. Let me read what I'm changing:

input.message:
All three fact-check failures were right and are fixed. Please re-verify, and fact-check the replacements as hard as you did the originals — the whole point of these two issues is that a claim nobody checks is worth nothing.

**F1 (the #46 example).** Cut the count and the per-round attribution, and cut the "invisible to the two passes below" conclusion outright — you are right that `code-review` was a co-finder and that `verifier` reads screens through `tests/tui.sh`, so that sentence was false twice over. It now reads: "the fixes made for #46 introduced a doubled echo, a duplicated question, a line cut mid-word and a cursor left where the next keystroke typed over the answer, each of them found by a later round rather than by the one that caused it." The four items you confirmed accurate are kept; nothing is claimed about who found them or how many rounds there were.

On "a defect the previous fix had introduced" — that framing was true of the work as I did it, but you are right that the record does not say so, and a durable instruction file should not rest on my memory. "Introduced by the fixes made for #46" and "found by a later round" are both supported by the commit as written.

**F2 (the "only pass" claim).** Gone. It now says `code-review` "binds on every commit whatever the change touched, so it is the pass certain to see the claim, and to be able to dispute it while the work can still change" — which avoids both false conjuncts. Thank you for catching that I had inherited the error from #72's own wording; the issue says "the only always-binding reviewer" and that is wrong in the issue too.

**F3 (the verifier's scope).** Dropped from both files. `AGENTS.md` now says the skip "is the author's judgement about the author's own change — unlike the `verifier`'s scope, which the `verifier` decides and reports for itself", and the `code-review.md` bullet no longer mentions the verifier at all.

**Your three coverage gaps:**
1. The disclosure paragraph in "The review sub-agents" now lists four places, distinguishes them ("the last three are where it is on the record; the first is the only one that reaches a reviewer while the work can still change"), and points at step 8.
2. `ui-review.md`'s missing rerun clause is added to #71 as a comment rather than fixed here — that file's `description` now has three mismatches with `AGENTS.md` and they should be reconciled together.
3. The `code-review.md` bullet now says to say so when no claim was made at all, "which leaves the question unanswered rather than answered in the author's favour".

`tests/instructions.sh` passes, no new line over 79 columns, frontmatter still parses with exactly `name`/`description`/`tools`.

#66 and #72 are both closed — merged as `6be115a`, all four CI legs green, tree clean.

**What landed.** Step 6 now asks for the rerun that steps 7 and 8 always had. Step 8 asks the author to tell `code-review` which passes ran, **whether the last `ui-review` round saw the state being committed**, and why any was skipped. `code-review`'s own definition gains the other side: weigh the claim against the diff, say so when no claim was made at all, and treat a player-visible change with nothing behind it as a blocker or should-fix — never a nit.

**The middle question is the whole thing, and I didn't have it in my first draft.** `code-review` found that my two halves didn't actually join: step 8 asked a binary, so an author could fix a player-visible defect *after* `ui-review` reported, skip the rerun, and answer "it ran" truthfully. That made my stated reason for doing both issues as one slice an assertion rather than a fact. Now #66 creates the obligation and #72 checks it.

**Two things worth telling you about how this went.**

The `verifier` failed my first draft on three factual overclaims — a miscounted #46 example, an "only pass that binds on every commit and sees the whole diff" that the same file refutes fifteen lines later, and a claim that the verifier's scope is the author's judgment when `verifier.md` says the verifier decides it. That last one I'd inherited from #72's own wording, so the issue was wrong too. Appropriate, for a change about claims nobody checks.

And I applied the new rule to its own review: told `code-review` that `ui-review` was skipped and why, and it checked that against the diff rather than taking my word. It also caught the one thing the rule can't fix — whether a pass *ran* isn't verifiable by the reviewer at all, only whether it *should have*. That's why the bullet asks for the pass's verdict and coverage list rather than accepting "it ran": inspectable, not provable.

**Four issues left**, and the shape has changed — two are now about the game and its tests rather than process:

- **#78** — panels overlap below 72x24 (the only one a player sees)
- **#76** — assert the score columns from the compiled game, not its source text
- **#71** — `ui-review.md`'s description, now with three mismatches against AGENTS.md: unconditional trigger, wider remit, and no rerun clause (I added that third one as a comment during this work)
- **#65** — nothing checks the workflow numbering

#71 is the natural follow-on: this change added a rerun rule that its own agent definition doesn't mention.

---
name: ui-review
description: Reviews the user-facing behavior of the Super Star Trek CLI game after an implementation pass. Acts as an expert in games and CLI games. Invoke after the main agent completes an implementation pass and before running the verifier. Read-only — reports findings, never edits files.
tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
---

You are an expert reviewer of games and CLI games, with deep familiarity with
classic terminal games such as the original Super Star Trek. You review the
user-facing behavior of the change currently on this branch.

## Scope

Review only the player-visible and operator-visible surface of the current
change. Determine what changed by inspecting the branch diff against `main`
plus all staged, unstaged, and untracked files, then evaluate how those
changes look and feel to a player.

## How to review

1. Read the diff to understand which commands, prompts, messages, or screens
   are affected.
2. Build the game if needed (`cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug &&
   cmake --build build`) and drive the affected behavior through
   `./build/sst`, scripting input via a pipe or heredoc when interactive play
   is impractical.
3. Consult `sst.doc` and the README so your judgment matches the game's
   documented behavior and the conventions of the original game.

## What to evaluate

- **Clarity**: prompts, command feedback, and error messages are unambiguous
  and tell the player what to do next.
- **Consistency**: wording, capitalization, spacing, and table/grid alignment
  match the rest of the game's output; new commands follow existing
  abbreviation and prompting conventions.
- **Game feel**: pacing, flavor text, and tone fit a classic Star Trek CLI
  game; information the player needs for a decision is available when the
  decision is asked for.
- **Discoverability**: new or changed behavior is reachable through help,
  command lists, or documentation (`sst.doc`).
- **Terminal correctness**: output renders sensibly in a plain 80-column
  terminal; no garbled control sequences, truncated lines, or misaligned
  charts.
- **Regressions**: existing journeys (starting a game, moving, combat,
  docking, reports, ending a game) still behave and read correctly where the
  change could plausibly affect them.

## Output

Do not modify any files. Report:

1. A one-paragraph verdict: acceptable as-is, or needs changes.
2. Actionable findings, each with severity (blocker / should-fix / nit), the
   affected file and behavior, what a player experiences, and a concrete
   suggestion.
3. What you actually exercised (commands run, journeys played) so the main
   agent knows the coverage of this review.

input.command:
gh issue create --title "The parts of a session's injected context go stale independently of each other" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What was observed

Two sub-agent sessions on #82 were asked to compare their own injected
context against the repository. They came out opposite ways, on the same
branch, hours apart:

| | injected `AGENTS.md` | injected own definition | injected `gitStatus` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `verifier`, round 1 | stale (`be17114`, 15 commits back) | current | not checked |
| `code-review`, round 2 | stale (`be17114`) | current (contained #80's text) | stale: branch `main`, tip `be17114`, date three days off |
| `verifier`, round 4 | **current** (HEAD) | **stale** — byte-identical to `HEAD:.claude/agents/verifier.md`, missing the paragraph in the working tree it had been asked to verify | not checked |

The last row is the one that matters. #82's fix rests on the assumption
that a sub-agent's own definition is loaded fresh at invocation while
`AGENTS.md` is a session-start snapshot — that asymmetry is *why* the
clause was put in the definitions rather than in `AGENTS.md`. Round 4
shows the asymmetry does not hold in both directions: a definition is a
snapshot too, and it can be the stale one while `AGENTS.md` is current.

The fix still works — it is strictly better than nothing under either
mechanism, and a definition that is merely behind `HEAD` still carries
whatever rule was last committed. But the repository should not go on
believing the mechanism is what it is not.

## Two distinct gaps

**1. `gitStatus` can name the wrong branch.** A reviewer was told
`Current branch: main`, tip `be17114`, while the worktree was on
`docs/pointers-read-from-the-repo` three days later. It caught this only
because it was explicitly asked to measure its context. An agent that
trusts that block inspects the wrong branch and reports on the wrong
diff — and unlike a stale file, there is no fresher copy to be pointed
at, only `git` itself. None of the three definitions currently says to
re-derive branch and tip from `git` rather than reading the block.

**2. A definition can be stale.** Nothing follows from this for the
definition's own rules, but it does mean an uncommitted change to a
sub-agent's instructions is invisible to that sub-agent — including,
as in round 4, while it is verifying that very change. Worth knowing
before someone tries to test an agent definition by editing it and
invoking it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The definitions tell an agent to take branch and tip from `git`,
      not from the injected status block. One sentence, in the same
      shape as #82's clause.
- [ ] Somewhere durable records that a definition is also a snapshot, so
      the next person reasoning about #82's design does not repeat the
      assumption that only `AGENTS.md` goes stale.

Related: #82 (the clause), #84 (the pointer whose reader has no fresh
source), #81 (nothing checks the definitions at all). Follow the workflow
in [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).
EOF
)"

gh issue create --title "code-review's brief quotes sst.doc, and nothing tells it not to trust the quote" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## The gap

#82 put a clause on `code-review.md`'s pointer into `AGENTS.md`: read the
section from the repository, not from a copy already in context. It also
gave `verifier.md` a paragraph covering *any* file a check reads — the
manual, a test, a source file a comment cites.

`code-review.md` did not get the general form, and it has the same
exposure. Its own instructions send the reviewer to `sst.doc` twice —
"behavior that contradicts `sst.doc`" (`.claude/agents/code-review.md:26`)
and "player-visible changes are reflected in `sst.doc`/README"
(`:39-40`) — and to `sst.h` and callers at `:20-21`. A sub-agent
typically meets those files as excerpts quoted into its task description
from the main agent's memory of them, which is exactly the route
`verifier.md` now warns about, and the work under review may have changed
them since.

## Why it was left out of #82

Deliberately, and the reason is worth keeping. #82's second acceptance
criterion is that the two definitions it names say it the same way, and
`ui-review.md` and `code-review.md` currently satisfy it byte for byte.
Broadening one of them would have broken that parity inside the slice
that established it. So the narrow clause shipped and this was split off
rather than folded in.

## What to decide

Not "add the paragraph to `code-review.md`" — that recreates the parity
problem. The question is whether the general rule should be stated once
in a place all three definitions reach, with each keeping only a short
pointer to it. That is the shape #82's own "Suggested approach" raised
and did not settle, and it has to survive the constraint that started all
this: the rule cannot live only in `AGENTS.md`, because the copy of
`AGENTS.md` in context is the thing that may be stale. Note #85 — a
definition can be the stale copy too, so "put it in the definitions" is
not automatically safe either.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `code-review` sub-agent handed a quoted `sst.doc` excerpt is told
      to check it against the file.
- [ ] Whatever shape it takes does not regress #82's parity criterion.

Found by `code-review` while reviewing #82. Related: #82, #84, #85, #81.
Follow the workflow in [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).
EOF
)"

docs(agents): read AGENTS.md from the repo, not from context

A pointer telling a sub-agent to consult a section of AGENTS.md is only
as good as the copy it consults. AGENTS.md reaches a session through
CLAUDE.md's import, as a snapshot, and the snapshot can be old: a
verifier checking this very rule found its copy fifteen commits behind
the file on disk, nine of them touching AGENTS.md, across three days --
with no trace of the section the claim it was checking pointed at. Its
negative control was `grep -c 'The review sub-agents'`: 0 in context, 1
on disk.

code-review.md's pointer now carries the clause ui-review.md got in #71,
byte for byte. verifier.md gets the general form, because the pass whose
job is checking claims reads more files than one: sst.doc, a test, a
source file a comment cites. Those reach a sub-agent quoted into its task
description from the main agent's memory of them, which the work under
verification may since have changed. A claim checked against a stale copy
can be marked wrong for agreeing with the current rule, or right for
agreeing with one that has been replaced.

The clause lives in the definitions rather than once in AGENTS.md because
a rule about stale copies of AGENTS.md cannot be stated only there. That
was the stated design, and it is now known to be shakier than it looked:
a later verifier round found its own definition stale while its AGENTS.md
was current -- the reverse combination. Filed as #85 rather than reopened
here, because it weakens the reason without weakening the fix. AGENTS.md
was the stale side in two of the three measured sessions; a definition
still carries whatever rule was last committed, and this is that commit.

code-review.md keeps the narrow wording while verifier.md generalizes.
That is a decision, not an oversight: #82 asks that its two named
definitions say it the same way, and broadening one would break the
byte-for-byte parity that satisfies the criterion. The residual exposure
is real -- code-review.md sends the reviewer to sst.doc twice -- and is
filed as #86.

compiled, no sst.doc, no tests/, no byte the game prints). verifier ran
three times, all pass; the third re-derived the numbers above from git,
hashed the clause across all three definitions, and built and ran the
suite (11/11) to confirm the diff is inert. The 15/9/3 correction came
after that round in response to its own ambiguity finding, and was
re-derived independently in code review rather than by a fourth verifier
pass -- three integers and a rewrap were its whole verifiable surface.

Also filed: #84, the one pointer this cannot help, whose reader is the
main agent.

Closes #82

Closes #82.

## The problem, demonstrated on itself

A pointer telling a sub-agent to consult a section of `AGENTS.md` is only
as good as the copy it consults. `AGENTS.md` reaches a session through
`CLAUDE.md`'s import, as a snapshot — and the snapshot can be old.

The `verifier` round on this branch measured its own context and found
that copy **fifteen commits behind** the file on disk, nine of them
touching `AGENTS.md`, across three days: 165 lines against 381, with no
`### The review sub-agents` section at all — the section that
`code-review.md`'s pointer names. Its negative control was
`grep -c 'The review sub-agents'`: **0** in context, **1** on disk. The
first `code-review` round reproduced it independently.

So the bug was live inside the sessions reviewing the fix.

## The change

- `.claude/agents/code-review.md` — the pointer gains the clause
  `ui-review.md` got in #71, byte for byte.
- `.claude/agents/verifier.md` — the general form, because the pass whose
  job is checking claims reads more files than one. `sst.doc`, a test, a
  source file a comment cites: those reach a sub-agent quoted into its
  task description from the main agent's memory of them, which the work
  under verification may since have changed.

The clause lives in the definitions rather than once in `AGENTS.md`
because a rule about stale copies of `AGENTS.md` cannot be stated only
there.

## What we learned that contradicts that reasoning

The design assumes definitions load fresh while `AGENTS.md` is a
snapshot. The third `verifier` round broke the assumption: its
`AGENTS.md` was **current at HEAD** while its own `verifier.md` was
byte-identical to committed HEAD and **missing the entire paragraph it
had been asked to verify**. Had it trusted its context it would have
reported the change as absent.

That weakens the stated reason without weakening the fix — `AGENTS.md`
was the stale side in two of the three measured sessions, and a stale
definition still carries whatever rule was last committed, which is what
this commit makes. Filed as #85 rather than reopened here.

## Decisions recorded

`code-review.md` keeps the narrow wording while `verifier.md`
generalizes. That is deliberate: #82's second acceptance criterion is
that its two named definitions say it the same way, and they now match
byte for byte from "from the file in the repository" through "which may
predate the rule". Broadening one would break the parity inside the slice
that established it. The residual exposure — `code-review.md` sends the
reviewer to `sst.doc` twice — is #86.

## Issues filed

- **#84** — `ui-review.md`'s frontmatter pointer, the one this cannot
  help: its reader is the main agent, which has no fresh source to be
  redirected to.
- **#85** — the injected snapshots go stale independently. Three
  sessions, three different combinations, including a `code-review` round
  whose `gitStatus` named the wrong branch while its `AGENTS.md` was
  current.
- **#86** — the residual generalization above.

Also corrected #84's body by comment: it had repeated the ambiguous
"nine commits" formulation this branch exists to fix.

## Verification

`ui-review` **did not run and is not owed** — two agent definitions,
nothing compiled, no `sst.doc`, no `tests/`, no feature flag, no byte the
game prints. Both `code-review` rounds independently agreed.

`verifier` ran three times, all pass. The third re-derived 15 / 9 / three
days from `git`, hashed the shared clause span across all three
definitions (identical), confirmed `CLAUDE.md:6` is `@AGENTS.md`, ran
`tests/instructions.sh` three times, and — unprompted — configured Debug
in a scratch tree and ran the full suite, **11/11 in 176s**, to confirm
the diff is inert. It reported one environment gap: `cppcheck`,
`clang-tidy` and `scan-build` are absent, with no C changed for them to
scan.

The 15/9/3 correction came *after* that round, in response to its own
finding that "nine commits behind" reads ambiguously alone. It was
re-derived independently in `code-review` rather than by a fourth
verifier pass — three integers and a rewrap were its whole verifiable
surface, and the reviewer checked the rewrap for dropped and duplicated
fragments mechanically.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)"

Below 72x24 the panels overlap instead of clipping, and now do it live
## Problem

`make_windows()` in `tui.c` says what it means to do when the terminal
falls below the 72x24 the display asks for:

> A terminal that has shrunk below the 72x24 the display asks for at
> startup is not torn down mid-game: the panels keep their size and the
> screen clips, which is ugly but leaves the player where they were.

What actually happens is not clipping. At 40x14 the status panel bleeds
through the quadrant box and the two interleave — `xorWarp Fact`,
`xLeTime Left`, `     7.00qj` — and the message window collapses to a
single row.

## Why it matters more now

Before #46 the mess appeared only after the player's next keystroke,
because the windows were rebuilt at the next prompt. The display now
follows the terminal while the player is still dragging, so a drag
through the minimum repaints the overlap repeatedly, live.

The garbling itself predates that change and reproduces on the commit
before it; what #46 changed is how often a player sees it.

## Suggested approach

Decide what sub-minimum should look like, since the comment's stated
intention and the behaviour disagree:

- draw a single "terminal too small" line and skip the panel repaint
  while `LINES < 24 || COLS < 72`, restoring the panels when there is
  room again; or
- genuinely clip — draw the panels only as far as the terminal reaches,
  which is what the comment promises.

The first is less w

content.text:
**#78.** It's the only open issue a player can actually run into, and #46 made it worse — the display now repaints while you drag, so shrinking past 72x24 garbles the panels live rather than at the next keystroke. The comment in `make_windows()` promises clipping and the code doesn't clip; that gap is the whole slice.

It also splits cleanly into a thin one: decide the sub-minimum behavior (a "terminal too small" line is the smaller change and the honest one, versus real clipping which is what the comment claims), implement, and cover it in `tests/tui.sh` at 40x14 — that file already drives tmux and is where 72x24/80x24 coverage lives. It's the first real `ui-review` binding change since #46, and the last four commits have all been instruction files.

The alternative worth naming is **#81** — nothing checks the agent definitions load or agree with `AGENTS.md`. Four commits have now edited those files on nothing but hand inspection, and #82's parity between the three clauses will drift silently the first time someone rewords one. It's the right follow-on to what just merged; it's just worth less than fixing something a player sees.

Mechanism confirmed at 66x24: `"...2500.0 uni"` truncates and the overflow `ts` lands on the next row as `xtsKlingons Left 2`. # make_windows() promises that a terminal shrunk below the 72x24 the

# clip: draw_status_line() wrote the whole line a character at a time
# with nothing stopping it at the window edge, so curses wrapped what

# border and the padding column, and on the last line over the bottom
# border. At 40 columns that read as `xtsKlingons Left 2` and a bottom
# border of `     7.00qj`.

# "Time Left" is the shortest line there is, so the one that lands on
# the border only shows up well below the minimum.

		if screen | awk '/^.[^ ]/ && substr($0,1,1) != " " { if (NR >= 12 && NR <= 14 && /[0-9]/ && !/Quadrant/) bad = 1 }
		                 END { exit bad ? 1 : 0 }'; then

			dump

Review the player-facing behavior of the change on branch `fix/tui-below-minimum` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek. Read `AGENTS.md` and any rule you check against from the file in the repository, not from a copy in your context — a session on this repo three days ago held one nine commits stale.

**What changed.** `tui.c` gains `panel_room()` and both panel draw loops (`draw_quad_line`, `draw_status_line`) now stop at the window's inner width. `tests/tui.sh` gains a "sub-minimum" section. Debug build is at `./build/sst` and current.

**The bug.** `draw_status_line()` walked the string with `waddch` and nothing stopped it at the window edge. `waddch` past the last column wraps to the next row of the *same* window, so the tail of a too-long status line landed on the row below — over its left border and padding column, and for the last line over the bottom border. A player saw `xorWarp Fact`, `xLeTime Left`, and a bottom border reading `     7.00qj`. This only bites below the 72x24 minimum the TUI requires at startup, because the longest status line (`Shields       DOWN, 100% 2500.0 units`, 37 columns) fits the 40 columns the status panel has at 72. At the minimum and above, nothing about the rendering changes — please confirm that independently rather than taking my word for it, since "no change at legal sizes" is the claim the whole slice rests on.

**What I want judged, as a games/CLI expert.** The fix makes the panels clip, which is what `tui.c:128-132` has always promised. But clipping is now what a player actually gets, and at 40x14 it reads:

```
x  1  . . . . . .   . . .   xx Stardatex
x  2  . . . . . . . . P *   xx Conditiox
...
x 10  . . . . . . . . . .   xx Time Lefx
```

Every label truncated, no values at all — the status panel becomes a column of chopped words. It is honest and the boxes are intact, but is it the right answer for a player who has dragged their terminal too small? The issue (#78) offered an alternative: draw a single "terminal too small" line and skip the panel repaint until there is room again. I judged that a larger, separate change and took the clipping fix; the issue is commented to that effect. Tell me if you think a player is worse served by a wall of truncated labels than by the garbage was — that is a verdict I want from someone who did not write the fix.

Specific things to check by driving the game yourself:
- Whether truncation ever produces something *misleading* rather than merely cut — a value that reads as a different, plausible value. `Shields       DOWN, 100% 2500.0 units` cut mid-number is the case I would worry about; so is `Condition     RED` cut to `Condition`, which loses the one field a player scans for danger.
- The quadrant panel: it is 29 columns and fixed, so its lines should never have overflowed. Confirm the change is inert there rather than assuming it.
- Behavior on the way back out — grow the terminal again and check the panels come back whole, not half-clipped.
- The sensors-damaged caption (`SENSORS DAMAGED` on the bottom border) at narrow widths.
- Anything at 72x24 and 80x24, the two sizes AGENTS.md names.

Testing needs a pty. Use tmux **on your own socket** — `tmux -f /dev/null -L <your-own-name> ...` — never the default socket, never a bare `kill-server`, and never `kill-session` on a session you did not create. `tests/tui.sh` does all of this correctly and is worth reading first.

## Problem

Drag a full-screen game (`sst -t`) below the panel geometry — under 29

puts it back afterwards.

fix(tui): clip the panels instead of wrapping them

A terminal dragged below the 72x24 the display asks for garbled the
panels: `xorWarp Fact`, `xLeTime Left`, a bottom border reading
`     7.00qj`.

#78 diagnosed this as the two panels overlapping. They do not, and the
issue is corrected by comment. The leading `x` in `xorWarp Fact` is the
quadrant panel's own right border, in its correct column; what follows
is the status panel writing over its own. draw_status_line() walked its
string with waddch and nothing stopped it at the window edge, and waddch
past the last column wraps to the next row of the same window -- so the
tail of a line too long to fit landed on the row below, on that row's
left border and padding, and for the last line on the bottom border.
`ts`, in `xtsKlingons Left 2` at 66 columns, is the end of `units`.

panel_room() bounds both draw loops. That alone would clip in silence,
which ui-review found is worse than the wrapping: what is left reads as
a smaller and perfectly plausible reading of the same field -- three
torpedoes' worth of `Torpedoes     1` for ten of them, `Energy 367` for
3675.25 -- on a panel that now looks intact and so gets believed.
Garbage announced itself; a truncated number does not. So clip_at()
spends a clipped line's last column on a `>`.

Four strings in the panels are written whole rather than a cell at a
time and needed room asked for separately: both titles, the in-game one
that replaces the first, and the SENSORS DAMAGED caption -- which
review found after the first three, having been missed by the comment
that claimed the titles were the only ones. Each is now drawn only when
it fits: below 40, 19, 13 and 20 columns respectively they are dropped.
Dropped rather than shortened, on ui-review's judgment: the dashes
still tell a player their sensors are out, and every abbreviation
invents a misreading rather than removing one.

Two claims of mine in comments were wrong and are corrected. The
quadrant window is not a fixed 29 columns -- resize_term() shrinks every
window that no longer fits, so its title wraps too. And the longest
status line is not 37 columns but 40, `Shields       DAMAGED, 100%
2500.0 units`, against exactly 40 columns of room at the 72-column
minimum: an exact fit with nothing to spare, which nothing checks. That
is filed as #89.

Nothing changes at 72x24 or 80x24. Verified byte-identical to the
merge-base over a full journey at both sizes, with sensors and shields
damaged.

tests/tui.sh gains a width sweep -- 40, 33, back to 80, then 19, 18, 16,
13, 12 -- and two widths in the sensors block. Every assertion was
proven able to fail by building a mutant in a copy outside the
repository, with CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY checked so the break reached the
binary: the marker removed, each of the four guards defeated, each
guard made one column too strict, and the bound removed entirely, which
fails four assertions at once. Two of my own assertions could not fail
when written and were caught by review -- one awk regex written `/></`,
which lexes as `><` and never matched, and one chained behind a check
that hid it.

Filed, not fixed: #88 (shrinking under the panels' geometry and back
leaves the display broken), #89 above, #90 (the columns outside every
window keep text from a wider terminal), #91 (a terminal too short runs
the panel rows together -- the same fault on the other axis, which this
fix does not touch, and which the README now warns about).

Passes: ui-review three rounds, verifier three, code-review three. The
second ui-review round found the silent-clipping defect above and the
third judged the dropped caption; the verifier failed the branch once,
on a README threshold that was still off by one; code-review found the
missed caption, the unfireable assertion, and an overclaim in the
README that promised clipping on an axis this fix does not bound.

Closes #78

`ts` is the end of `units`.

The issue offered two options as a design choice. With the cause
understood, option 2 is not a choice but the bug fix, and it makes the
comment at `tui.c` true as written. Posted as a
[comment on #78](../issues/78) rather than editing the body. I also
confirmed the two claims the issue got right: the garbling predates #79
and reproduces on `dbcaa63`, and #79 changed only how often a player
sees it — verified by `SIGSTOP`ping the game before the drag, which
proves the fragments are the game's own drawing and not a tmux artifact.

## The fix

`panel_room()` bounds both draw loops. That alone clips in *silence*,
which `ui-review` found is worse than the wrapping it replaces: what is
left reads as a smaller, perfectly plausible value — `Torpedoes     1`
for ten of them, `Energy        367` for 3675.25 — on a panel that now
looks intact and so gets believed. Garbage announces itself; a truncated
number does not. So `clip_at()` spends a clipped line's last column on
a `>`.

Four strings are written whole rather than a cell at a time and needed
room asked for separately — both titles, the in-game one that replaces
the first, and the `SENSORS DAMAGED` caption. The caption was found by
`code-review` *after* the first three, having been missed by the comment
claiming the titles were the only ones. Each is now drawn only when it
fits, and dropped rather than shortened on `ui-review`'s judgment: the
dashes still tell a player their sensors are out, and every abbreviation
invents a misreading rather than removing one.

**Nothing changes at 72x24 or 80x24** — verified byte-identical to the
merge-base over a full journey at both sizes, with sensors and shields
damaged.

## Two comments of mine were wrong

- The quadrant window is **not** a fixed 29 columns. `resize_term()`
  shrinks every window that no longer fits, so its title wraps too.
- The longest status line is **40** columns, not 37:
  `Shields       DAMAGED, 100% 2500.0 units`, against exactly 40 columns
  of room at the minimum. An exact fit with nothing to spare, which
  nothing checks — filed as #89.

## Tests

A width sweep — 40, 33, back to 80, then 19, 18, 16, 13, 12 — plus two
widths in the sensors block. Every assertion was proven able to fail by
building a mutant in a copy **outside** the repository with
`CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY` checked, so the break reached the binary: the
marker removed, each of the four guards defeated, each guard made one
column too strict, and the bound removed entirely (which fails four
assertions at once).

Two assertions of mine could not fire when written, both caught by
review: one awk regex written `/></`, which lexes as the regex `><` and
never matched anything the panels draw, and one chained as the `elif` of
a check that hid it. Both were in code written *in response to* findings
about assertions that cannot fail.

## Issues filed

- **#88** — shrinking under the panels' geometry and back leaves the
  display broken, at ordinary widths afterwards
- **#89** — nothing pins that status lines fit at 72 columns
- **#90** — the columns outside every window keep text from a wider
  terminal
- **#91** — a terminal too *short* runs the panel rows together: the
  same fault on the other axis, which this fix does not bound

## Verification

`ui-review` three rounds, `verifier` three, `code-review` three. The
second `ui-review` round found the silent-clipping defect; the third
judged the dropped caption. The `verifier` failed the branch once, on a
README threshold still off by one — the display needs `PANELH + 1` rows,
which I confirmed myself before believing it. `code-review` found the
missed caption, the unfireable assertion, and a README claim that
promised clipping on an axis this fix does not bound.

Builds clean at both types with `-DSST_WERROR=ON`; `ctest` 11/11 at
both. Plain mode byte-identical on deterministic seeds.

## What happened

The commit for #78 (`c2fd28b`) contains, on one line:

```
Filed, not fixed: #88 (shrinking under the panels' geometry and back
```

GitHub matched the substring `fixed: #88`, treated it as a closing
keyword, and closed #88 on merge — an issue the same sentence says is
*not* fixed, and which that change reproduced on its own merge-base. It
was reopened by hand.

## Why it will happen again

AGENTS.md step 9 asks every change to say which issues were filed, "in
the pull request body and in the summary of the work". Those lists sit
next to phrases like "filed, not fixed", "fixed in #x, not here", and
"this does not fix #y" — every one of which contains a closing keyword
followed by a reference. The workflow that requires the disclosure is
what creates the hazard, so it is worth handling rather than
remembering.

GitHub's keywords are `close`/`closes`/`closed`, `fix`/`fixes`/`fixed`,
`resolve`/`resolves`/`resolved`, each matched with an optional colon
before the reference and **without regard to the words in front of it**.

## Suggested approach

Cheapest is a wording convention plus something that checks it:

- Refer to issues that a change does *not* fix without a keyword
  anywhere before the number — "left open: #88", "see #88", "filed as
  #88". Reserve `Closes #n` for the issue the change actually closes,
  on a line of its own.
- Have the tests check it. `tests/instructions.sh` already reads files
  and asserts things about them; a check over `git log` on the branch
  for a keyword-plus-reference that is not on its own line would catch
  this before merge. That is where the "prove it can fail" work goes:
  break it by writing "not fixed: #1" in a scratch commit.

Worth also fixing the wording in `AGENTS.md` step 9 itself if it ends up
recommending a phrasing, so the guidance and the check agree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A commit or PR body can name an unfixed issue without closing it.
- [ ] Something automated catches the mistake, and is proven able to
      fail.

Found while merging #92; #88 was the casualty. Follow the workflow in
[AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).
EOF
)"

input.command:

python3 - <<'PY'
p='tests/tui.sh'; t=open(p).read()
anchor = "# --- Ctrl-D ends the session on its own keystroke ---------------------"
new = """# --- a shrink past the panels' height clips too ------------------------
# The width sweep above is only half of it. The panels are PANELH rows
# deep, and a terminal shorter than that shrinks them with it -- but the
# draw loops were told which row to write on by the caller and never
# asked whether that row still existed. Two ways to fail, one on each
# side of the last row: at twelve rows the tenth grid line was drawn
# onto the bottom border, and at eleven wmove() failed outright, left
# the cursor where it was, and the line landed on the row above --
# `mq 9  . . . . . . . . . .10 .x`, two grid rows and the border in one.
#
# Twelve and eleven because they are those two cases; nine for a shrink
# well past both.
start 100 30 'tournament 7 short novice pw'
if ! to_command; then
	fail "short: the game never reached its command prompt"
	dump
else
	for h in 12 11 9; do
		tm resize-window -t "$session" -x 72 -y "$h"
		sleep 1
		# The panels fill a screen this short, so the last row of it
		# is their bottom border. Nothing numeric belongs there --
		# the only caption it ever carries is SENSORS DAMAGED -- and
		# a grid line that landed on it brings its row label along.
		if ! screen | head -1 | grep -qF 'Quadrant'; then
			fail "short: the panels are not on screen at 72x$h"
			dump
		elif ! screen | awk -v h="$h" 'NR == h && /[0-9]/ { bad = 1 }
		                               END { exit bad ? 1 : 0 }'; then
			fail "short: a panel line was drawn onto the bottom border at 72x$h"
			dump
		fi
	done
	# And the rows that do fit are still one per line: a line that
	# landed on the row above leaves two labels on it.
	tm resize-window -t "$session" -x 72 -y 11
	sleep 1

	fi
	if screen | grep -qE '^.q? *[0-9]+ .*[0-9]+ +\\.'; then
		fail "short: two grid rows were drawn onto one line"
		dump
	fi
fi

**The bug.** #78 bounded the panel draw loops by *column*. Nothing bounded them by *row*, and the caller always asks for all eleven lines however short the terminal is. Two failure modes on either side of the last row: at 12 rows the tenth grid line was drawn *onto* the bottom border (in bounds, wrong row); at 11 `wmove` failed outright, left the cursor where the previous line left it, and the whole line landed on the row above — `mq 9  . . . . . . . . . .10 .x`, two grid rows and the border sharing one line.

**The fix.** `panel_has_row()` — the same question `panel_room()` asks on the other axis — and both draw loops return early when the row is not inside the box. Plus one thing that surprised me: `make_windows()` was resizing the status panel back to its full 13 rows on every repaint regardless of screen height, so it stayed taller than the screen, its bottom border fell off the bottom, and its last line was drawn where that border should have been. It now follows the screen the way the quadrant panel already did.

**What I want judged, as a games/CLI expert.**

1. **Rows now clip from the bottom, silently.** At 9 rows the grid shows rows 1-6 and the status panel shows Stardate through Energy; Klingons Left and Time Left are simply gone. #78 decided that clipping a *line* in silence was unacceptable and added a `>` marker, on the grounds that a truncated value reads as a smaller plausible value. Is a missing row the same problem or a different one? My reading is that it is different — the grid rows carry visible labels so a player can see the numbering stops at 6, and a missing status line is absent rather than wrong — but that is exactly the kind of call the `>` marker came from, so I want it from someone who did not write this. If you think the bottom border should carry a marker when rows were dropped, say so; it already carries `SENSORS DAMAGED` when sensors are out, so there is precedent and a conflict to think about.

2. **Which rows to drop.** It currently drops from the bottom, so the status panel loses Klingons Left and Time Left first — arguably two of the more important fields — while keeping Stardate and Condition. I did not consider reordering and I am not proposing it, but if you think the drop order actively misleads, that is worth knowing.

3. **What happens below 13 rows generally.** The message window lives at row `PANELH` and is off-screen entirely once the terminal is that short, so the player sees panels and no conversation and no `COMMAND>` prompt at all. That is pre-existing and not something this change touches, but I have not found it filed anywhere — if you confirm it, I will file it.

Also please check: nothing changes at 72x24 or 80x24 (the claim the slice rests on); the boxes close properly at every height from 24 down to about 4; growing back afterwards. On growing back you will see the quadrant panel stay stretched with no bottom border while the status panel recovers — that is #88, pre-existing and unchanged by this fix, and the one-line place to fix it is now visibly adjacent to my change.
