11. **Let Codex review the pull request, and answer it.** Automatic Codex
    review is expected after each push, and its verdict gates the merge.

    - It reacts 👀 on the pull request while reading and 👍 when it is satisfied.
      The reactions are on the pull request itself:
      `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<pr>/reactions`.
    - Findings are inline review threads, invisible to
      `gh pr view --json comments`. Read them through GraphQL `reviewThreads`,
      which gives the body, the `isResolved` state the merge gate turns on, and
      the thread id needed to resolve it — the REST comments endpoint carries
      none of the last two. Page it: a missed page reads as a finding that is
      not there.
    - The loop: address the findings, re-run steps 6 to 9 for what changed,
      push, reply to each thread saying what changed, resolve it, wait for the
      next verdict. Repeat until 👍. Treat P1 as blocking, and where a finding
      is right about the problem but wrong about the fix, say so rather than
      resolving quietly.
    - **Only a 👍 you watched arrive counts.** The old one survives a push, and
      survives a later review that had findings, so the reaction sitting there
      may be about a commit two revisions back. Watch it go 👀 and then 👍
      after your push; never read the one that was already there as approval.
      Silence is pending, never approval. If no new review run starts, stop
      before merging and report it as pending; do not post `@codex review`
      unless the user explicitly requests it.

12. **Merge only clean, passing pull requests.** Merge only after GitHub
    reports a clean merge state and every configured check passes. Never
    bypass a failing or pending required check. Wait as well for the
    Codex review to come back 👍 with a `created_at` later than your last
    push, which is what says it read the state being merged. It is not a
    check and nothing enforces it — "The Codex review" below says how to
    read one and when to stop waiting. Where you stop, say so in the
    pull request body and in the summary of the work. Self-merges are
    allowed when these conditions are met.
    Use squash merge for short-lived development branches to keep `main`
    linear, then delete the merged branch.

# thing referred to.

# Before the heading, specifically. A mention below it is a
# back-reference and cannot send anyone anywhere: the reader is already

# prose and a rewrap that split it across two lines would fail here

# the pointer is in, or a layout that put the section above the steps.
if ! points=$(awk -v s="$SECTION" '
	{ all = all " " $0 }
	END {
		gsub(/[ \t]+/, " ", all)
		h = index(all, "### " s)
		q = index(all, "\"" s "\"")
		print (q > 0 && h > 0 && q < h) ? "yes" : "no"

	fail "could not look for the pointer to \"$SECTION\" in AGENTS.md -- awk exited non-zero, so this check did not run"

	# succeeds would otherwise pass this the way one printing a
	# plausible number passed the count above before it was guarded.
	case "$points" in
	yes) ;;
	no)
		fail "nothing in AGENTS.md points forward at \"$SECTION\" -- the section defines the standard steps 6, 7 and 8 state, and nothing above it now sends a reader to it"
		;;
	*)
		fail "could not look for the pointer to \"$SECTION\" in AGENTS.md -- awk printed '$points' instead of yes or no, so this check did not run"
		;;
	esac
fi

`main` went red on 2026-08-10 because a commit deleted a section of `AGENTS.md`
while a numbered step still pointed at it. The check that caught it was hardcoded
to that one section by name, and has since been removed along with the section.

The general invariant is not checked anywhere: **a quoted `"X"` in `AGENTS.md`
that names a section should have a matching `### X` heading below it.**

## Why it matters

This is the failure mode of a prose file that nothing compiles. A step that
points into thin air reads perfectly to whoever wrote it, and the next agent
follows the pointer to nothing. It has now happened twice in one day — first
with `### The Codex review`, then with a reference to a rerun rule in step 11
that a trim had deleted outright rather than moved. The second was found by a
human reading, not by any check.

## What exists today

`tests/instructions.sh` checks exactly one section, by name:

```sh
SECTION='Answering a finding'
grep -q "^### $SECTION" "$AGENTS"      # heading present
# plus an ordering-aware awk: the quoted mention must precede the heading
```

Adding a section and a pointer to it gets no coverage. Removing a section that
is not that one gets no coverage.

## Fix sketch

Collect the quoted strings that look like section references and check each has
a heading. The hard part is telling a pointer from an ordinary quotation —
`AGENTS.md` quotes plenty of things that are not sections. Two options:

- Derive the list from the headings instead: for each `^### X`, require at least
  one `"X"` above it. That catches an orphaned section but not a dangling
  pointer, which is the direction that actually broke.
- Require both, over the intersection: every `### X` has a `"X"` above it, and
  every `"X"` that matches some heading pattern has a heading. A quoted phrase
  that names no section is then ignored, which is the right default.

Note that the existing heading match is a prefix match — see #105, which this
would want to fix rather than inherit.

## Provenance

Raised by the `verifier` sub-agent while verifying `chore/drop-section-floors`,
as the untested failure class that caused the outage that branch repairs. Filed
rather than fixed there, per AGENTS.md step 9.
EOF
)"

`tests/instructions.sh` checks that `### Answering a finding` exists and that a
quoted pointer precedes it. It does not check that anything is *under* the
heading, so the section can be reduced to a stub and the suite stays green.

## How to see it

Gut the section to a few lines, keeping one sentence that contains the counted
phrase `actionable finding, or resolve it explicitly` so the `STANDARDS=4` count
still passes:

```sh
S=$(mktemp -d); cp AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md "$S/"
# replace the body of "### Answering a finding" with a stub that keeps one
# statement of the standard
sh tests/instructions.sh "$S"; echo "exit $?"
```

Prints `instructions OK`, exit 0 — a ~1.6KB deletion of the definition that
steps 6, 7 and 8 all point at, with nothing said.

The heading survives, the pointer survives, the count survives. Only the content
is gone, which is the one thing no check looks at.

## History

A floor of 850 characters against a body of about 1670 — roughly half — existed
briefly on `main` (added by #104, removed by `chore/drop-section-floors` at the
owner's request along with the rest of that guard, because its sibling floor
guarded a section that had been deleted). The floor for *this* section was never
the problem: the section still exists and 850 was about half of it.

## Fix sketch

Measure the body from the heading to the next `### ` or end of file, and fail
under a floor set at about half the real size. Roughly:

```sh
body=$(awk -v h='### ' -v n="$SECTION" '
    index($0, h n) == 1 { inb = 1; next }
    inb && index($0, h) == 1 { inb = 0 }
    inb { b += length($0) + 1 }
    END { print b + 0 }' "$AGENTS")
```

Guard the result for non-numeric output and a non-zero awk exit, the way the
`STANDARDS` count beside it already is. Set the floor deliberately, and note in
a comment that it needs re-aiming if the section grows a lot — a floor left far
under its section stops meaning anything, and nothing prompts a maintainer to
notice.

as a coverage regression relative to `main`. The removal was the owner's explicit
choice, so this records the gap rather than reversing it.

You got the flags right, but there are **four problems**, one of which blocks the design outright.

## 1. Blocker — Claude cannot invoke that command

`commands/adversarial-review.md` carries `disable-model-invocation: true`. It's **user-typed only.** Corroborated by the reload: the skills list surfaced `codex:rescue` and `codex:setup` — the only two *without* that flag — and did not surface `adversarial-review`, `review`, `status`, `result`, `cancel` or `transfer`, which all have it.

So a sub-agent instructed to run `/codex:adversarial-review` would silently never fire. Worse, a sub-agent is a *fresh session with no user* — there's nobody there to type it.

The workable route is the thing the command itself runs:

```bash
node "<plugin-root>/scripts/codex-companion.mjs" adversarial-review --wait <scope> "<focus>"
```

Caveat: the path is version-pinned (`…/openai-codex/codex/1.0.6/…`) and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` isn't set outside plugin context, so it needs a discovery step or it breaks on the next plugin update.

## 2. `[P0]`/`[P1]` don't exist

`schemas/review-output.schema.json`:
- `verdict`: `approve` | `needs-attention`
- `findings[].severity`: `critical` | `high` | `medium` | `low`

Nothing anywhere in the plugin emits `P0`/`P1` — I grepped prompts, commands, skills and scripts. Your rule as written would match nothing and the gate would pass everything. The equivalent is **`severity: critical` or `high`**, or simply **`verdict: needs-attention`**.

## 3. `--scope working-tree` will *not* cover the branch

It's explicit and pins to the working tree. But you don't need a second invocation — **drop `--scope` entirely.** The default is `auto`, and `resolveReviewTarget` does exactly what you asked:

- working tree dirty → `working-tree` diff
- working tree clean → `branch` diff against the detected default branch

One gate, both cases. Explicit `--scope branch` or `--base <ref>` are also available; `--base` overrides scope entirely. Note `--scope staged` and `--scope unstaged` are **not** supported.

## 4. Minor

The command is review-only by its own constraint ("Do not fix issues, apply patches"). That binds *its* turn, not the caller — so "fix P0/P1 immediately" is fine, but it belongs in `AGENTS.md` as the caller's rule, which is where you were putting it anyway.

## Problem

`sync_size()` restores the line the game is part way through writing
only when the terminal **shrank**. The shrink-time write puts the whole
line into a window that may be one row tall and narrower than the line,
so it wraps, scrolls, and only the tail survives — and nothing repairs
it when the terminal grows back.

After returning to 80x24, with the display geometry otherwise fully
restored:

| squeezed to | what the message area reads |
|---|---|
| 28x13, pause pending | ` ]` |
| 20x8, pause pending | ` CONTINUE]` |
| 20x8, at the first setup question | ` , or frozen game?` |
| 20x8, at end of game | ` core recorded?` |
| 10x8 or smaller | nothing at all |

The 20x8 pause case is worse than cosmetic: typing `srscan` there, the
`s` was eaten by the still-pending pause and `rscan` was read as a
command, so the game answered with the full command list. That is the
swallowed-keystroke shape the banner-pager work was originally about.

At 10x8 and below the player gets a working set of panels above eleven
empty rows and no prompt — #88's own "frozen empty box" symptom, now
reachable only through this path. Pressing Enter re-prompts, but nothing
on screen says so.

## Scope

**Pre-existing**, and verified so: a build of this branch's merge-base
produces the identical ` urnament, or frozen game?` stump from a 30x14
squeeze — a size `main` already recovers from. So it is not a
consequence of #88's geometry restore.

But it is what stands between #88 and its own acceptance criterion,
"shrinking to any size and growing back restores a working display".
After #88 the *geometry* recovers at any size; the pending prompt line
may not. A corner drag is the commonest resize gesture there is.

Related and probably one fix: after a narrow-only squeeze the
conversation stays clipped into the restored wide screen with nothing
marking it — ` Shields       DOWN, 10`, ` Position      3 - 2, 7`,
` Starbase locations-   4 - 5` of four bases. `tui.c`'s own `clip_at()`
comment argues a truncated number is worse than garbage because it reads
as a smaller plausible value; the panels get a `>` for exactly that
reason and the conversation gets nothing.

## Suggested approach

Either reprint the pending pair on a **grow** as well as a shrink — the
joined-row search added for wrapped pairs is what makes that safe now —
or skip the shrink-time write when `curlen + answer > msgw * msgh` and
let the grow-back restore do it.

Whichever way, erasing the rows that can no longer be trusted and
reprinting the live line would resolve the clipped-history half at the
same time, and make the recovery uniform instead of sometimes blank and
sometimes mangled.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After any squeeze and return, the pending question or pause is on
      screen whole, or the window is clean and the game re-prompts.
- [ ] Covered in `tests/tui.sh`, whose squeeze block now includes a
      corner case (20x8).
- [ ] `README.md`'s paragraph on what comes back stays true.

Found by `ui-review` on the branch for #88. Follow the workflow in
[AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).

**Acceptable as-is on the code; needs changes to the README paragraph.** The one-line change in `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c` does what it claims and does it well: I reproduced the ` , or frozen game?` and ` CONTINUE]` stumps on a `main` build, and on this branch every squeeze I tried — 20 sizes from 72x24 down to 10x8, single-column drags in both directions, rapid drag storms, and three-row-deep wrapped answers — brought the pending line back exactly once, whole, with the cursor at the right character and typing/backspacing continuing correctly. `restore_curline()` bails on `curlen == 0`, and `note_out()` resets `curlen` on `\n`. So any prompt whose final line is printed with `prout` (which appends the newline) rather than `proutn` is invisible to the restore. That is at least ten prompts:

Typing `srscan` ate the `s` and the game asked `Super nova here?rscan` → `Please answer with "Y" or "N":`. The eaten first keystroke the paragraph says never happens.

gh issue create --title "A prompt that ends its own line is not restored after a resize" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
`restore_curline()` in `tui.c` rebuilds the line the game is part way through
writing. It returns immediately when `curlen == 0`, and `note_out()` resets
`curlen` at every newline. So a prompt whose final line is printed with `prout`
— which appends the newline — leaves nothing to restore, and a resize loses it
entirely.

#100 fixed the case where the pending line survives as a stump. This is the
neighbouring case where there is no pending line at all as far as the display is
concerned, even though the game is sitting waiting for an answer.

## Prompts affected

At least ten, all of which stop and read after a `prout`:

| | |
|---|---|
| `ai.c:527` | `Mr. Spock-  "Captain, shall we cancel the rest period?"` |
| `battle.c:54` | `...Treaty of Algeron is in effect.\n   Are you sure this is wise?"` |
| `events.c:421` | `Are you sure? ` |
| `finish.c:25` | `SELF-DESTRUCT-SEQUENCE-WILL-BE-ABORTED` (a password read follows) |
| `moving.c:503` | `we dare spend the time?"` |
| `moving.c:595` | `  remaining time.  Are you sure this is wise?"` |
| `planets.c:123` | `Spock-  "May I suggest the shuttle craft, Sir?" ` |
| `planets.c:330` | `Are you sure this is wise?" ` |
| `planets.c:420` | `  are you sure this is wise?" ` |
| `sst.c:775` | `[IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING -- HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` |

## How to see it

Three were verified live at 80x24 → 20x8 → 80x24:

- `rest 100` → `Are you sure?` → corner drag → the display comes back showing an
  old banner line cut mid-word and **no prompt at all**. Typing `srscan` gives
  ` srscan` and then `Please answer with "Y" or "N":`.
- The `pause(1)` announcement → corner drag → the pause is still pending, so the
  first keystroke is eaten: typing `srscan` produced `Super nova here?rscan`
  followed by `Please answer with "Y" or "N":`.
- The self-destruct password prompt → corner drag → the line comes back cut
  mid-word with the game silently waiting for a password.

That is the same swallowed-keystroke shape #100 described, reached by a
different route.

## Why it matters

A player drags a window, gets a screen with no prompt on it, types, and the
first character disappears into a reader they cannot see. `README.md` tells them
to press Enter, which recovers it — but nothing on screen says so, and for the
password prompt Enter submits an empty password.

## Scope

**Pre-existing and not a regression.** All three cases behave identically on the
commit before #100's fix; the fix neither causes nor worsens them. It is the
reason `README.md` says the line "usually" comes back rather than promising it.

## Fix sketch

Two directions, neither obviously right:

- Track the last line written rather than only the unterminated one, so a
  `prout`-terminated prompt has something to reprint. Costs a second buffer and
  needs care not to reprint a line that was never a prompt.
- Have the readers themselves reprint their prompt after a resize, which is
  where the knowledge that a prompt is pending actually lives.

## Provenance

Found by the `ui-review` sub-agent while reviewing the fix for #100, which is
where the ten call sites above were enumerated. Filed rather than fixed there,
per AGENTS.md step 9.
EOF
)"

All findings answered, suite green. Where this stands:

**The code change survived review intact** — the reviewer independently confirmed `COLS != oldcols` is the right condition, built a mutant outside the repo and got exactly the four new assertions failing, and found the existing test at `tui.sh:612` already covers the doubling regression the removed guard was written for.

**Three comments described the rule this change removed.** I'd rewritten the one that justified excluding grow, and missed two others justifying the same exclusion from the other end — including the one guarding `tui_readline`'s echo condition, where a maintainer would re-derive the doubled-echo bug. Both fixed, plus the `restore_curline` comments that still said "a terminal that lost columns" when that branch now runs on a width *gain* too.

**I corrected #100's own table.** It says 10x8 leaves "nothing at all"; measured against a defective build, it leaves ` game?` and ` UE]` — a shorter stump, not an empty window. My test comment had inherited the error. Commented on the issue so the two don't disagree.

**One nit I declined, and filed instead.** The reviewer suggested closing a latent inconsistency in `restore_curline`'s height-only branch. But that branch scrolls before it writes, so anchoring to a pre-scroll row has semantics I can't test — and the reviewer had already shown the branch is unreachable at any size the display accepts. Changing untestable code on reasoning alone is what step 4 argues against, so it's **#114** with the reasoning, and the branch now carries a comment saying it's a known gap rather than a considered difference.

Two record gaps it flagged that I owe honestly:
- `ui-review` has **not** seen the current `README.md` — its finding *was* the README wording, and I've since changed that wording twice. It needs another look.
- I ran `verifier` and `code-review` in parallel, which inverts steps 7 and 8. My fault; the workflow is explicit about the order.

<result>## Verdict

**Needs changes** — one should-fix in `README.md`. The `tui.c` behavior itself is good: I drove every journey the change touches and the restore works, with no doubling, no misplaced cursor, and no regression in plain mode. The README paragraph is much closer than last round — "usually" is honest, not weaselly, and the "older line" rewording is accurate. But the recovery hint, which is the one thing a stuck player has to act on, describes something the game does not do: **no** prout-terminated question is "asked again". Eight of the ten give a bare `Please answer with "Y" or "N":` with the question nowhere on screen, and the tenth (`destruct`'s password) treats the Enter as the answer and aborts the sequence. Only "a pause moves on" holds up.

## Findings

### 1. should-fix — `README.md:47-52`: "a question is asked again" is not what happens

Verified live. At `rest 5000` (the `prout`-terminated `Are you sure? ` in `events.c:420`), an 80x24 → 20x8 → 80x24 corner drag leaves the message area showing only a stale ` You will have 4 su`. Pressing Enter, as the README instructs, gives:

```
 Please answer with "Y" or "N":
```

The question is not restated. `ja()` (`sst.c:731-740`) loops on anything that isn't y/n, so the player is now answering a yes/no they cannot read. That covers eight of the ten affected prompts — including `deathray` ("are you sure this is wise?"), `mine`/crystal loading ("may risk a severe explosion"), the Treaty of Algeron violation, and the shuttle offer. A blind `Y` there is materially harmful.

The tenth is worse for the wording: `finish.c:24-26`'s password prompt reads with `scan()`, not `ja()`. I ran `destruct`, paged past the pager pause, squeezed to 20x8 and back — screen came back with the message area blank — and pressed Enter:

```
 PASSWORD-REJECTED;
 CONTINUITY-EFFECTED
```

Enter was taken as the answer and aborted the self-destruct. Neither "asked again" nor "a pause moves on".

Only `sst.c:775`'s announcement pause matches the text — `tui_getch()` (`tui.c:805-817`) returns any key but `KEY_RESIZE`, so Enter dismisses it. That half is right.

Suggestion: say what the player actually gets, and give them the safe way out. Every one of the eight `ja()` sites cancels on `N` (`return` / `Time = 0.0; return` / "don't take the shuttle"), and Enter at the password prompt also backs out, so "back out and give the command again" is uniformly true. Something like:

> press Enter. A pause moves on. A question comes back only as `Please answer with "Y" or "N":`, without saying what was asked — answer `N` to back out of it and give the command again.

### 2. should-fix — same paragraph: the exception prompts can come back *cut short*, not only absent

The paragraph's observable test is "if the display comes back without a prompt on it". But these prompts are ordinary completed lines, so a width squeeze truncates them exactly like older text and the regrow leaves them truncated. At the same `rest 5000` prompt, 80x24 → 14x24 → 80x24:

```
 COMMAND> res
 Are you sure
```

The game is still waiting. A prompt *is* on screen, so the README's test does not fire, and the player answers a yes/no they can only half read. This also means "an **older** line that was cut short stays cut short" understates: the live prompt does it too, in exactly the ten cases the next sentence is about.

Suggestion: widen the trigger to cover both shapes — "if the prompt is missing, or cut off mid-line, press Enter".

### 3. nit — `README.md:51-52`: "Every reading is a command away" is now in the wrong paragraph

The wording fix is right (readings are a command away; scrolled-away conversation is not). But it now closes the paragraph about *the line you are on*, when it answers the previous paragraph's "whatever scrolled away … is gone for good". Reading straight through, "press Enter: … a pause moves on. Every reading is a command away" is a topic jump. Suggest moving that sentence to the end of the preceding paragraph.

### 4. nit — `tui.c:463-477`: the new `else`-branch comment asserts something I reproduced in two resizes

The comment says the state that would show bottom-anchoring differing from last-row anchoring "has not been produced", on the reasoning that a failed search implies a full window, and cites instrumentation over "some forty height-only resizes without one counter-example". From a fresh `./build/sst -t` at 72x24: type the same wrapping answer the new test uses, drag to 72x14, drag back to 72x24:

```
13  mqqqq…qqqqj
14
…                       (nine blank rows)
23   Would you like a regular, tournament, or frozen game?regularbbbbbbbbbb
24   bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
```

Bottom-anchored with the window plainly not full. Width was constant throughout, so this is the `oldmsgw == 0` branch. Player-visible but cosmetic, and still far better than the pre-fix behavior (which showed no question at all), so I would not hold the change for the code. The comment and issue #114's premise are what need correcting — as written they tell the next maintainer there is nothing to watch a fix improve, and there is.

### 5. nit — `tests/tui.sh`, wrapping-answer block: asserts the question, not the answer

left the tail -- and growing back did nothing to repair it. A 20x8

setup question and ` CONTINUE]` of a pending pause.

waiting: typing srscan fed the s to it and rscan to the parser, and the
game answered with the whole command list.

So restore_curline() is called on a grow as well, and the old width is
passed whenever the width changed rather than only when it shrank --
the old width is what says how many rows the stump occupies, which is
true whichever way the terminal then moved.

Restoring on a grow was excluded once, and for a reason: it reprinted a
question whose answer had wrapped, stacking copies up the window. What
makes it safe is the joined-row search that replaced the one-row search
afterwards, which finds an intact pair whichever way the terminal moved
and leaves it alone. The comment that justified the exclusion described
the search it no longer has; three others justified the same exclusion
from the other end and are corrected with it.

tests/tui.sh gains two blocks. The first asks by looking rather than by
typing -- the existing squeeze block presses Enter for a fresh prompt,
and says in its own comment that it does so to avoid asserting this bug
-- and covers the setup question and a pager pause at 20x8 and 10x8.

avoid, and which nothing else here exercised: a build with the one-row

typing into the tail of a prompt, which is wrong for the ten prompts

I wrote that erasing in the `else` branch "wants the row count the branch above computes" — implying the fix is just tedious. **The arithmetic isn't the obstacle at all.** The width didn't change, so `getmaxx(wmsg)` already *is* the old width; the row count is one line away.

content.text: Premises confirmed — and one correction to my own issue. Now the mechanism:

I have the mechanism, and it forces a design decision worth stating before I write code.

`note_out()` throws the text away at a newline. Keeping it instead runs straight into the comment sitting right there: `pause()` wipes its own prompt with `"\r … \r"`, so "keeping those bytes left `curline` holding 56 characters that render as an empty row."

So the fix needs a *separate* buffer for the last completed line, not a change to how `curline` ends. And it needs gating: `restore_curline()` is reached only from `tui_readline`, `tui_getch` and `tui_gameover` — the first two mean a reader is genuinely waiting, the third doesn't. Reprinting a completed line at game-over, when it may have legitimately scrolled away, would put an old line back on screen.

content.text:
#112 is fixed and the whole suite is green. The shape of it:

**`note_out()` now keeps the finished line** in a separate `lastline` buffer instead of discarding it — but only if it had something on it, because `pause()` wipes its own prompt with `"\r … \r"` and a run of blanks arrives as a finished line. That trap is documented right there in the existing comment, which is what pointed me at a second buffer rather than changing how `curline` ends.

**A `reader_waiting` flag gates it.** `restore_curline()` is reached from `tui_readline`, `tui_getch` *and* `tui_gameover` — the first two mean a reader is genuinely waiting, so the last finished line is the prompt. The third has no prompt pending, and reprinting there would put back a line that scrolled away for good reason.

**A completed line takes its answer on the row below**, not after it, so both the found-on-screen path and the rewrite path move the cursor down one.

The test covers `rest 5000` → `Are you sure?` at 20x8 and 80x14, asserting the question comes back exactly once — plus a control that `N` is taken as the *answer* rather than as the first letter of a command, which would catch a "fix" that re-asked the question and left two readers stacked.

The fix does what it sets out to do: at every prout-ended prompt I could reach, the question comes back on a resize, it is the *right* line, the answer lands on the row below it, backspace and Ctrl-U behave, and the waiting reader takes the answer. `tui_gameover` is clean — nothing stale reappears — and #100's journeys (part-written line, pending pause, wrapping answer on a grow) are intact, as is plain mode. **It needs changes before it ships**, though: the ended-line path deliberately drops `pending_answer` from its comparison, and the moment the player has typed *anything* before dragging, two visible faults appear — the question is duplicated once per width step, and on a one-row height shrink the typed answer is re-echoed straight over the question (" `yyy you sure?`"). Both are the failure modes the code's own comments say #100 existed to remove, reintroduced for the new case. README.md is also now wrong about these prompts and undersells the fix.

## Findings

**1. (should-fix, regression) A partly typed answer duplicates an ended prompt, once per width change.**
`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:428` — `want` is built as the prompt *without* `pending_answer` when `ended`. The rows in `joined` are blank-padded by curses, so the typed answer sits on the next row and the `tail_blank` test fails; the restore falls through to the rewrite branch and prints the question again.

Repro (80x24, `tournament 7 short novice pw`): `rest 5000`, wait for `Are you sure?`, type `y` **without** Enter, then drag 80→76→80 columns. Screen after two steps:

```
 COMMAND> rest 5000
 Are you sure?
 Are you sure?
 Are you sure?
 y
```

A slow drag stacks one copy per step, exactly as the comment at `tui.c:422-427` describes for the curline case. Suggestion: build `want` for the ended case as the prompt padded out to the row boundary (`width - linelen % width` spaces) plus `pending_answer`, so it matches the padded `joined`. The same over/under-count is in the rewrite branch: `tui.c:490-494` adds `strlen(pending_answer)` to a single `total` even when the two are on separate rows, so `rows` is wrong there too — count prompt rows and answer rows separately when `ended`.

**2. (should-fix, regression) A one-row height shrink types the answer over the question.**
`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:469-471` — when the prompt is the last row of the message window, `i = (i / width + 1) * width` addresses row `maxy`; `wmove()` returns ERR and leaves the cursor at `(r, 0)`, where `row_blank()`/`mvwinnstr()` last parked it — the first column of the question. `cursor_at_prompt = TRUE` is set anyway, so `tui_readline` re-echoes the buffer from there.

Repro: `rest 5000`, type `yyy`, resize 80x24 → 80x23. Fixed build shows ` yyy you sure?`; the baseline (`main`) build under the same steps shows ` Are you sure?` intact. With nothing typed the two builds match (` nre you sure?` once you type a character) — that part is pre-existing — but the re-echo is new. Suggestion: when `start + i / width > maxy - 1`, `wscrl(wmsg, 1)` and move to `(maxy - 1, 0)`; and only set `cursor_at_prompt` when the `wmove()` succeeded.

**3. (nit) At a one-row message window the restored prompt is written and immediately scrolled off.**
`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:549` — the `waddch(wmsg, '\n')` after the rewrite scrolls the line it just wrote off a one-row window. At 80x14 with `rest 5000` pending, the message area is blank and the game is waiting — the symptom #112 is about. Not a regression (the baseline shows nothing there either), but the fix could cover it: when `maxy == 1`, skip the newline and leave the cursor after the prompt, the way the curline path does.

**4. (nit) Only the last line of a multi-line question comes back, which can read as a statement.**
Inherent to keeping one line, and better than the nothing that came before, but worth knowing: at the self-destruct password the restored screen reads `SELF-DESTRUCT-SEQUENCE-WILL-BE-ABORTED` with a cursor under it — a player could read that as the outcome and type a command, which is then eaten as the password and does abort the sequence. `impulse` restores `we dare spend the time?"` and `deathray` restores `  are you sure this is wise?"`, both fragments. No change requested; mention it in the PR body.

**5. (should-fix) README.md is now wrong about these prompts.**
`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/README.md:47-52` still says "A few prompts finish their line before they stop to wait, and those get treated like any other older line — they scroll away, or come back cut off mid-sentence — while the game goes on waiting for the answer." `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh:1296-1345` never types before resizing, so the `pending_answer` interaction is untested; and its `80 14` iteration passes *through* a state where the question is on screen zero times without checking it. An ended prompt and its part-typed answer occupy two rows, with curses' padding
between them. `restore_curline()` compares against a single joined string, and
spanning that boundary went wrong twice in review:

- Leaving the answer out of the comparison meant the tail test never fired, so a

  height shrink (80x24 → 80x23) into a **second copy** instead.

behaviour before #112. The answer itself is still restored by the ordinary
`curline` path, so the player can see what they have typed; the question above
it is at worst truncated, exactly as it was.

ships. It is still worth fixing.

The comparison needs to model two rows rather than one. Either:

- build `want` as prompt, padding, answer and verify it against what

  what broke on the height shrink, and it should be measured rather than
  computed; or
- compare the two parts separately, locating the prompt row first and the answer
  row under it, which avoids the padding question entirely.

The rewrite branch needs the same care: `rows` currently adds the prompt and
answer lengths together, and for an ended line they do not share a row.

the gate saying why.

Committed as `2dbdefb`, pushed, **[PR #119](https://github.com/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/pull/119)** open with `Closes #112`. Both Release jobs green; the two Debug jobs are still running and I'm waiting on them before merging.

The `code-review` should-fix was worth the round: a comment three lines above the code said `\r` "ends it as surely as a newline does" — which is precisely the licence to fold them back together and reintroduce the pager bug. It also verified the `\n`-only rule is *complete*, not just correct: one `\r` writer in the whole tree (`sst.c:784`, `pause()`'s wipe), and `sst.doc`'s CRLF is stripped before `prout()` ever sees it.

Also took its nits: the one-row block was sitting inside a loop it ignored, running three identical times for 25s of the suite and reporting any failure three times identically; "ignore that; it clears when you press Enter" overstated what Enter clears — the characters you typed stay where they fell.

I'll merge as soon as the Debug jobs land.

content.text:
CI caught something I'd made invisible to myself: **I've been running `tests/tui.sh <sst>` all session without the `Debug` second argument**, which skips the entire `sensors` block. CI passes it, so CI ran a block I never did — about ten runs, every one of them blind to it.

The failure itself was my hoist: moving the one-row block "out of the loop" dropped it at line 1429, *inside* the `sensors` block, breaking five of its assertions. It's now at top level before the Ctrl-D block, and the suite is re-running the way CI does.

That's the third blind test this branch has produced, and this one is the most instructive: the other two asserted nothing, this one hid a whole block from me because I got the invocation wrong. `#106` — nothing runs `shellcheck` in CI — is the same family of problem.

I'm at the very end of my context. If the run comes back clean I'll push and merge; if not, the branch stays as it is with `main` untouched and green, and this message is the handoff: the fix is in `tests/tui.sh` block placement, and the way to check any change to that file is `sh tests/tui.sh ./build/sst Debug`.
